[ADVOCATE NAME], Advocate
[CHAMBERS ADDRESS] | Email: [EMAIL] | Tel: [PHONE] | Enrolment No. [ENROLMENT NUMBER]

Ref. No.: [REF]/2026                                              Date: [DATE OF NOTICE]
BY REGISTERED POST A.D. AND BY EMAIL

To,
Ms. Akriti Swaroop
[TENANTED PREMISES ADDRESS], being the residential apartment let out to her by my Client
(Also sent to email ID: [TENANT EMAIL ADDRESS], if available)

Sub: Legal notice demanding payment of arrears of rent amounting to Rs. 96,000/- (Rupees Ninety-Six Thousand only) for the months of May, June and July 2026, and calling upon you to remedy the said breach of the Lease Agreement dated 15.01.2026 within 15 (fifteen) days, failing which my Client shall be constrained to determine the tenancy and initiate appropriate legal proceedings.

Sir/Madam,

Under instructions from and on behalf of my Client, Ms. Karuna Anupam (hereinafter referred to as "my Client"), I address you as follows:

1. That my Client is the absolute owner and landlord of the residential apartment situated at [PROPERTY ADDRESS] (hereinafter referred to as "the tenanted premises").

2. That by a Lease Agreement dated 15.01.2026 ("the Lease Agreement"), my Client let out the tenanted premises to you on a monthly rent of Rs. 32,000/- (Rupees Thirty-Two Thousand only), payable in advance on or before the [DAY] day of each English calendar month, the tenancy being a month-to-month tenancy commencing on 15.01.2026. The precise terms as to the due date for payment of rent, and any clause of the Lease Agreement bearing on notice or termination, are as recorded in the Lease Agreement, a copy of which is asserted by my Client to be in her possession.

3. That you have failed and neglected to pay rent for the months of May 2026, June 2026 and July 2026, despite the same having fallen due, whereby a sum of Rs. 96,000/- (Rupees Ninety-Six Thousand only), being three (3) months' rent at Rs. 32,000/- (Rupees Thirty-Two Thousand only) per month, has fallen due and remains unpaid and outstanding as on the date of this notice.

4. That my Client has, on several occasions prior to the issuance of this notice, requested and reminded you, both orally and otherwise, to clear the said outstanding dues, which reminders you have failed and neglected to heed. Particulars of the specific dates of such prior reminders are asserted by my Client and are to be confirmed and set out with precision before this notice is finalised.

5. That your aforesaid non-payment of rent for three consecutive months constitutes a breach of the terms of the Lease Agreement dated 15.01.2026 and disentitles you to continue in occupation of the tenanted premises as a tenant in good standing.

6. That the cause of action for this notice arose in the first instance when the rent for May 2026 fell due and remained unpaid, and arose further and continuously when the rent for June 2026 and July 2026 respectively fell due and remained unpaid, and the cause of action is continuing and subsisting as on the date of this notice.

That without prejudice to the demand for arrears made herein, and in the event the outstanding dues and consequences set out below are not complied with within the period stipulated, my Client determines your tenancy in respect of the tenanted premises under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, by this notice. The tenancy having commenced on the 15th day of the month, a month of the tenancy runs from the 15th day of one calendar month to the 14th day of the succeeding calendar month; accordingly, this notice shall operate to determine your tenancy with effect from the expiry of the 14th day of [MONTH], 2026, being the last day of a month of the tenancy reckoned from the date of commencement, and you are called upon to deliver vacant and peaceful possession of the tenanted premises on the expiry of that date. Whether the local Rent Control Act applicable to the State in which the tenanted premises are situated excludes or restricts the operation of Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, and prescribes its own grounds and procedure for eviction, has not been ascertained; the applicable State Rent Control Act (exact statute and section to be confirmed) shall govern to the extent it applies, and this determination is made without prejudice to my Client's rights and remedies under that Act.

TAKE NOTICE that in the event of your failure to comply with the demands made hereinabove within the period of 15 (fifteen) days aforesaid, my Client shall be constrained to initiate appropriate civil proceedings against you for recovery of the arrears of rent, mesne profits/damages for use and occupation, and for eviction and recovery of vacant and peaceful possession of the tenanted premises, under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the applicable State Rent Control Act (exact statute and section to be confirmed), the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, and/or the Specific Relief Act, 1963, as may be applicable, before the competent court or authority having jurisdiction, entirely at your risk as to costs and consequences. Without prejudice to the foregoing, my Client expressly reserves all rights and remedies available to her in law and in equity.

Yours faithfully,

[ADVOCATE NAME]
Advocate
Counsel for Ms. Karuna Anupam

A copy of this notice is retained in my office for further necessary action.

assumptions.assumption: The tenanted premises address has not been provided and is placed as a bracketed placeholder.
assumptions.why: No property address was given in the instructions.

assumptions.assumption: The tenancy is treated as a month-to-month tenancy commencing on the 15th of each month, and the due date for rent is assumed to fall on the 15th day of each month, mirroring the lease commencement date.
assumptions.why: The instructions state the lease is dated 15 January 2026 but do not specify the rent due date or whether the tenancy is month-to-month; this is necessary to compute the s.106 notice expiry.

assumptions.assumption: The State in which the premises are situated, and therefore the applicable State Rent Control Act, has not been identified and is left as a named-but-unspecified statute marked for confirmation.
assumptions.why: No State was mentioned in the instructions and rent control is a State subject that may override s.106 TP Act.

assumptions.assumption: The dates and mode of the 'repeated reminders' referred to in the instructions have been generalised in the notice rather than particularised with specific dates.
assumptions.why: The instructions assert repeated reminders were given but do not supply dates or mode.

assumptions.assumption: The rate of interest claimed on arrears has not been fixed and is left to be governed by the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and/or the Lease Agreement rather than a specific stated percentage.
assumptions.why: No interest rate or lease clause on interest was supplied.

assumptions.assumption: The cost of notice has been placed at Rs. 5,500/- as a representative figure.
assumptions.why: No figure for cost of notice was supplied by the client; this is a standard placeholder figure used in practice but must be confirmed or adjusted.

assumptions.assumption: The advocate's name, chambers address, email, phone, enrolment number and reference number are all placeholders.

drafting_notes.issue: The exact due date of rent each month and the precise day the tenancy commenced (for computing month-of-tenancy under s.106 TP Act) were not supplied; only the Lease Agreement date of 15.01.2026 was given.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Obtain the Lease Agreement and confirm the contractual due date for rent and the exact day of the month the tenancy is deemed to commence, so the determination date in this notice can be fixed with certainty rather than assumed.

drafting_notes.issue: The State in which the premises are situated has not been identified, so the applicable State Rent Control Act could not be named, and it is unknown whether that Act excludes or modifies s.106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 or prescribes specific grounds/procedure for eviction.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Ascertain the State and the specific Rent Control Act applicable to the premises before this notice is finalised and served, and confirm the exact section governing termination and eviction under that Act.

drafting_notes.issue: The instructions describe the non-payment as a 'breach of the lease agreement' and ask only for a demand and 15-day compliance period; they do not expressly instruct determination of the tenancy or eviction. This draft, per the mandatory skeleton for this document type, has additionally determined the tenancy and demanded vacant possession as an alternative/without-prejudice measure.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Confirm with the client whether she intends only to demand arrears and continue the tenancy if paid, or whether she also intends to terminate the tenancy now. The notice as drafted keeps both options open (arrears demand plus without-prejudice determination), which should be reviewed against the client's actual intention before service.

drafting_notes.issue: No lease clause regarding interest on delayed rent, mesne profits rate, or notice-cost recovery was supplied.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Check the Lease Agreement for any specific clause on interest, damages for delay, or notice costs, and amend the NOW THEREFORE clause to reflect the contractual rate rather than a generic reference to the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

drafting_notes.issue: Specific dates of the 'repeated reminders' asserted by the client were not provided.
drafting_notes.recommendation: Obtain specific dates and mode (oral/written/WhatsApp/email) of each prior reminder from the client and insert them in paragraph 4 to strengthen the evidentiary record for any future proceeding.

drafting_notes.issue: This is a civil rent-arrears/eviction matter; no penal-law references have been used anywhere in this notice, consistent with the mandate that this is a civil matter only.
drafting_notes.recommendation: No action needed; noted for the file that the statute policy has been complied with.
